The short grievance of the Petitioners, regardless of the text of the prayer in the pleadings is as to non- extension of enhanced compensation otherwise payable under Section 29 of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner banks upon the decision of a Coordinate Bench of this Court in SMT. RUKMINI & ANOTHER vs THE STATE OF KARNATAKA & OTHERS in W.P.No.39611-39612/2016 (LA- KIADB) disposed off on 16.09.2016.

sentences.text: 2. Learned AGA appears for the 1st Respondent and the learned Panel Counsel appearing for the Respondent - KIADB vehemently oppose the Petition contending that the petitioners' claim squarely falls in General Award Category and not under Section 29(2) of the Act; they have already accordingly received entire compensation; therefore, they cannot be granted any relief at the hands of Writ Court.
So contending, they seek dismissal of the Writ Petition.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court is although broadly in agreement with the submission of learned AGA and the Panel Counsel appearing for the KIADB, permits the petitioners to file a representation seeking enhanced benefit in terms of Section 29(2) of the 1966 Act, provided that in similar cases such a benefit has been accorded by the KIADB even when the case fell in the General Award category.
If such a representation is made, KIADB would consider the same in accordance with law and within a period of three months.
It is open to the Petitioners to lay a claim for the developed portion of the land in terms of Government Notification in lieu of compensation.
Writ petition is disposed off accordingly, keeping open all contentions.
No costs.

opennyai_summary.decision:
So contending, they seek dismissal of the Writ Petition.
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court is although broadly in agreement with the submission of learned AGA and the Panel Counsel appearing for the KIADB, permits the petitioners to file a representation seeking enhanced benefit in terms of Section 29(2) of the 1966 Act, provided that in similar cases such a benefit has been accorded by the KIADB even when the case fell in the General Award category.
If such a representation is made, KIADB would consider the same in accordance with law and within a period of three months.
It is open to the Petitioners to lay a claim for the developed portion of the land in terms of Government Notification in lieu of compensation.
Writ petition is disposed off accordingly, keeping open all contentions.
